items.title: Define the closed scope-defining and closeout-evidence artifact classifications
items.context: Register trusted lifecycle paths and canonical writer provenance while preserving existing scope-contract classification. Explicitly exclude the milestone-closeout-only registration owned by B-9188 unless it has merged.
items.userSees: User runs the M4.C1 contract verifier and sees `PASS closeout artifact classifications: closed set and canonical writer provenance verified`; adding an unknown trusted path or wrong writer makes the command exit non-zero with the exact path.

happy.desc: The M4.C1 contract verifier enumerates a closed set of scope-defining and closeout-evidence artifact paths, preserves the existing scope-contract class, and reports canonical writer provenance for every trusted path.

edge.desc: The verifier rejects an unknown lifecycle artifact path and a known path written by a non-canonical command, exits non-zero, and names the offending path and writer.

adversarial.desc: A path cannot become trusted through prefix, basename, traversal, symlink, alias, or broad-whitelist matching; milestone-closeout-only ownership remains excluded unless B-9188 has merged and registered it canonically.

items.title: Add a composite scope-defining digest and re-attestation boundary
items.context: Digest semantically relevant scope acknowledgements/provenance, milestone ledger, and slice plan so metadata-only closeout cannot reuse review evidence from storyFilesHash alone.
items.userSees: User sees `PASS composite scope digest: semantic scope facts bound`; changing acknowledgement content/provenance, milestone ledger, or slice plan changes the digest and blocks metadata-only review retention until signed re-attestation.

happy.desc: The composite scope-defining digest deterministically binds the normalized scope acknowledgement content, its canonical writer provenance, the milestone ledger, and the slice plan, and identical semantic inputs reproduce the same digest.

edge.desc: Changing any one bound input—acknowledgement content, acknowledgement provenance, milestone ledger, or slice plan—changes the composite digest and blocks metadata-only review retention pending fresh signed re-attestation.

adversarial.desc: Reordering keys, rewriting only an embedded claimed digest, replaying an old acknowledgement with different provenance, or substituting an unbound ledger/plan cannot preserve or spoof the composite digest.

items.title: Validate trusted persisted artifact schemas and embedded hashes
items.context: Before using milestone ledger, plan, parent rollup, or delivery context as a trust boundary, schema-validate and recompute ledgerHash, planHash, rollupHash, and delivery-context structure.
items.userSees: User sees `PASS trusted closeout artifacts: schema and embedded hashes verified`; a malformed ledger/plan/rollup/delivery-context artifact or forged embedded hash is rejected with a named artifact error.

happy.desc: Before trust-boundary use, valid milestone-ledger, slice-plan, parent-rollup, and delivery-context artifacts pass their runtime schemas and independently recomputed ledgerHash, planHash, and rollupHash checks.

edge.desc: Each artifact class fails closed with a named artifact and reason when required fields are missing, types/versions are invalid, or its recomputed embedded hash differs from the persisted claim.

adversarial.desc: An attacker cannot gain trust by changing payload and embedded hash together under a non-canonical schema, using duplicate/extra ambiguity, cross-story substitution, stale provenance, or a structurally plausible but semantically invalid delivery context.

items.title: Keep canonical TEST closeout writes from creating synthetic scope expansion
items.context: A canonical parent_ledger_rollup_set with unchanged product/material diff and composite scope digest must remain in TEST; source/test/docs or semantic scope changes must still force DEV/REVIEW.
items.userSees: User runs the TEST roll-up regression and sees `PASS canonical closeout write retained TEST`; the paired source/docs/scope mutations visibly route back to DEV/REVIEW.

happy.desc: In TEST, canonical parent_ledger_rollup_set output with unchanged product/material diff and unchanged composite scope digest remains in TEST and reports PASS canonical closeout write retained TEST.

edge.desc: Paired mutations to a source, test, or documentation file, or to any semantic scope fact, are distinguished from canonical rollup-only metadata and route the story back to DEV/REVIEW as appropriate.

adversarial.desc: A manually written, wrong-writer, malformed, hash-forged, unknown-path, or mixed rollup-plus-material change cannot masquerade as canonical TEST closeout or suppress synthetic scope-expansion detection.

items.title: Add fail-closed regression coverage for metadata-only review retention
items.context: Cover unknown paths, changed product files, changed scope facts, missing provenance/hash/schema, and new review-round pass reuse; retain command-policy rejection of scope_contract_acknowledge in TEST.
items.userSees: User runs the M4.C1 regression suite and sees `PASS metadata-only review retention is fail-closed`; unknown paths, changed material/scope, missing provenance, malformed hashes, TEST acknowledgement, and new-round pass reuse are all rejected.

happy.desc: Metadata-only review retention succeeds only when all four conditions hold together: every changed path is a registered closeout-evidence path, product/material diff is unchanged, the composite scope-defining digest is unchanged, and canonical provenance plus schema/recomputed-hash validation passes.

edge.desc: The regression suite independently negates each retention condition—unknown path, changed product/material file, changed scope fact/digest, and missing or invalid provenance/schema/hash—and every case fails closed; scope_contract_acknowledge remains rejected in TEST.

adversarial.desc: A pass from an earlier review round is never inherited by a new round, even when HEAD, storyFilesHash, or closeout metadata appear unchanged; replayed/stale pass IDs and combined metadata mutations cannot satisfy current-round review assurance.
